# Properties of the Gamma Function

The Gamma Function is defined as:

$$ \Gamma(z) = \int_0^\infty t^{z-1} e^{-t} \, dt, \quad \Re(z) > 0 $$

It extends the factorial function such that:

$$ \Gamma(n) = (n-1)! $$

and satisfies the recursive property:

$$ \Gamma(z+1) = z \, \Gamma(z). $$

---

```{r gamma-function-demo, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Load libraries
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Evaluate Gamma function at some points
z_vals <- c(0.5, 1, 2, 3, 3.5, 5)
gamma_vals <- gamma(z_vals)

results <- data.frame(z = z_vals,
                      Gamma_z = gamma_vals,
                      Check = c(sqrt(pi), 1, 1, 2, NA, 24))

results

# 2. Verify the recursive property Γ(z+1) = zΓ(z)
z_test <- 2.5
lhs <- gamma(z_test + 1)
rhs <- z_test * gamma(z_test)

cat("Check recursive property for z =", z_test, "\n")
cat("Γ(z+1) =", lhs, " | z*Γ(z) =", rhs, "\n")

# 3. Plot the Gamma function
x <- seq(0.1, 5, length.out = 200)
y <- gamma(x)

df <- data.frame(x = x, y = y)

# Factorial values at integers
ints <- 1:5
fact_points <- data.frame(x = ints, y = gamma(ints))

ggplot(df, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue", size = 1) +
  geom_point(data = fact_points, aes(x, y), color = "red", size = 3) +
  geom_text(data = fact_points,
            aes(x, y, label = paste0(round(y, 1))),
            vjust = -1, color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Gamma Function Γ(x)",
       subtitle = "Red points = factorial values at integers",
       x = "x",
       y = "Γ(x)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
